notes: Hardware: ASUS Ascent GX10 (NVIDIA GB10, 128 GiB unified LPDDR5x; the census row 'DGX Spark 128GB' covers every GB10 128GB system — same memory pool and DGX OS reserve). 66.84 GiB = the sum of the runtime's own allocation lines in the attached 0.30.6 log (https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28686286/_ollama_logs.txt, sha256 above): CUDA0 model buffer 66,221.98 MiB + CUDA_Host model buffer 970.00 MiB + CUDA0 KV buffer 680.00 MiB + CUDA0 recurrent-state buffer 62.81 MiB + CUDA0 compute 360.30 MiB + CUDA_Host compute 144.30 MiB + CUDA_Host output 0.95 MiB = 68,440.34 MiB. Logged at context creation; llama.cpp sizes these buffers for the largest batch and keeps them for the run, so they are the runtime's working set during generation. NOT included: the CUDA context, process heap, the CPU-side vision encoder and its 248.10 MiB CPU compute buffer, llama-server's host prompt cache (size limit 8,192 MiB) and context checkpoints — on GB10 those share the same pool. Maintainer checks 2026-10-20: (1) physical consistency — model buffers 67,191.98 MiB = the logged GGUF file size 65.62 GiB (15.88 BPW, 41 blocks incl. the MTP layer); the KV buffer equals the hand count 65,536 x 10 full-attention layers x 2 (K,V) x 2 KV heads x 256 x 1.0625 B (q8_0) = 680.00 MiB exactly; (2) engine reproduction — fitllm 2.19.0-2.21.3 predicted weights 65.19 + KV 0.63 + state 0.06 + runtime 9.88 = 75.76 GiB (+13.4%), the runtime term being 12% of the weights (7.82) + 15% of KV (0.09) + 65,536 x 0.00003 (1.97); (3) the reporter measured their own machine (issue author); (4) raw artifact = the attached log.
